title: Monotonicity of tree circuit size
statement: Let $T,T':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and let $L$ be a language of Boolean words. If $L$ has Boolean circuit trees of size at most $T(n)$ that recognize it at each input length, and $T(n)\le T'(n)$ for every $n$, then $L$ also has such trees of size at most $T'(n)$ at every input length.
hypotheses_covered: $T,T'$ map natural numbers to natural numbers
$L$ is a language of Boolean words
$L$ has circuit trees of size at most $T(n)$ recognizing it at each length
